newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBAL-COWBOYS STAR DEFENSIVE TACKLE LETT GETS DRUG SUSPENSION.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBAL-COWBOYS STAR DEFENSIVE TACKLE LETT GETS DRUG SUSPENSION.

text.p: Dallas Cowboys star defensive tackle Leon Lett was suspended for one year Tuesday for failing a drug test, the National Football League announced.
It is the second time in as many seasons Lett has violated the league's substance-abuse policy. Lett, who was suspended for four games last season, reportedly tested positive for cocaine.

"This is a time of concern for Leon Lett the person," Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said in a statement. "Our thoughts are with him and his family, and we will continue to offer our help and support in any way we can."

According to NFL policy, a player suspended for a minimum of one year may apply for reinstatement no sooner than 60 days prior to the one-year anniversary date of the suspension. Lett is not allowed to participate with the team in any way during the suspension.

Last week, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reported that the failed drug test was Lett's 11th drug test in a month, one over the maximum under league rules. But NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue said he was satisfied with the process.

"I am fully satisfied that the program's test collection and processing arrangements, to which the NFL and NFL Players Association have agreed, fully ensure the integrity and accuracy of test results," Tagliabue said.

Lett appeared in all 13 games for Dallas this season, recording three sacks and recovering two fumbles. The sixth-year player has spent his entire career with Dallas, ammassing 13 1/2 sacks and establishing himself as one of the NFL's top run-stoppers.
His departure further thins a defence that is without injured defensive end Charles Haley and starting safety Brock Marion. The Cowboys have the top-ranked defence in the league.
Lett is the fifth different Cowboys' player to be suspended for violating the league's substance abuse policy in the past 18 months.

All-Pro receiver Michael Irvin was involved in a high-profile drug trial prior to the start of this season and was suspended for five games, and defensive lineman Shante Carver missed the opening six games for breaking league substance abuse by-laws.
Former defensive back Clayton Holmes and wide receiver Cory Fleming also have been suspended for drug violations.
